correctness.rationale: For alpha>0 and normalized f with zf′/f subordinate to exp, the universal radius is the largest R with exp(R D) inside v²<4alpha(u-1/2). The extremal canonical exponential function gives necessity. The leftmost point exp(-log2)=1/2 forces R<=L=log2. Expanding the boundary near -L yields y² coefficient alpha(1-L)/L-1/4, so for alpha<L/[4(1-L)] an interior off-axis violation forces R<L. At alpha*=L/[4(1-L)], the source proves global positivity using alternating trigonometric polynomial bounds on |z|<=L, monotonicity in U=y², and a rigorous exact-rational polynomial certificate for Q(t,L). An independently reconstructed SymPy/rational calculation verified the polynomial degree 17, log2 enclosure 0.693<L<0.694, constant coefficient >0.04684, negative terms <0.00023 and strict margin >0.0466. Thus exp(LD) contained in target for alpha>=alpha*. The proof is an infinite-disk inclusion with exact rational bounds, not a finite search. No exact radius below alpha* is claimed.
